questions.question: Why does Quayline run its background work from a Postgres table instead of a message broker?
questions.gold: ADR-0001 keeps all state in one Postgres database because the harbour office has one part-time administrator and every extra system is one more thing nobody will patch; background work is a jobs table polled with SKIP LOCKED.

questions.question: Does Quayline's berth allocation call the harbour authority's tide feed when it quotes a stay?
questions.gold: No. Since ADR-0003 a job fetches the next 30 days of predictions once an hour into tides.predictions, and allocation reads only that table, never the feed (the feed timed out most nights, #17).

questions.question: When several free berths could take a boat, which one does Quayline pick?
questions.gold: The smallest one that fits on every night of the stay, ties broken by the lowest berth code (ADR-0005). Fitting means length at least the boat's length plus 1 m, width at least the beam plus 0.4 m, and depth at the lowest low water at least the draft plus the clearance margin.

questions.question: Can a skipper choose a particular berth when booking through Quayline?
questions.gold: No. Quayline allocates the berth (ADR-0005); only the harbour office can move a booking by hand.

questions.question: What happens to Quayline's API routes when a breaking change is needed?
questions.gold: A /v2 prefix is added beside /v1, and /v1 stays for at least six months after /v2 ships; additive changes such as a new optional field stay in /v1 (ADR-0006).

questions.question: Do seasonal berth holders get priority on Quayline's visitor waitlist?
questions.gold: No. The waitlist is first come, first served by request time; the only exception is a vessel seeking refuge from weather, which goes to the front (ADR-0007).

questions.question: Why are Quayline's amounts integers, and at what point is a charge rounded?
questions.gold: Float sums were a penny out on about one stay in two hundred and the office reconciles to the penny (#52), so ADR-0008 stores every amount as integer pence (bigint columns, the Pence type). Rounding happens once, half up, when a night's charge is computed.

questions.question: Why did Quayline stop producing invoices in its 02:00 run?
questions.gold: Skippers who left in the morning waited a day for their invoice and a departure recorded after 02:00 slipped a further day (#76). ADR-0009 builds the invoice when the departure is recorded, emailed within the hour, and supersedes ADR-0002.

questions.question: Which Quayline messages still go out as text messages?
questions.gold: Only safety alerts (storm and tide warnings), sent to every vessel on site. Since ADR-0010, which superseded ADR-0004, confirmations, reminders and invoices go by email and push.

questions.question: Has Quayline adopted dynamic pricing for busy nights?
questions.gold: No. ADR-0011 is only proposed (up to 25% more above 90% booked, up to 15% less under 40%); the Trust's board has not agreed it and its draft, PR #160, is open.

questions.question: Which details about the boat must a Quayline booking capture?
questions.gold: The vessel's name, length overall, beam and draft, in metres to one decimal place (REQ-B1).

questions.question: How long does an unconfirmed Quayline booking keep its berth?
questions.gold: 15 minutes (REQ-B3); after that the hold is released and the berth is free again.

questions.question: What is the longest stay a visitor can book in Quayline?
questions.gold: 21 nights (REQ-B5). A longer stay needs a seasonal agreement, which the office sets up by hand.

questions.question: What does a skipper pay to cancel a Quayline booking the day before arrival?
questions.gold: The first night's charge: cancelling is free only more than 48 hours before arrival (REQ-B7).

questions.question: How is the boat length used for a Quayline nightly charge rounded?
questions.gold: Up to the next half metre of length overall (REQ-P1; charged_length_m).

questions.question: When does Quayline's winter rate apply, and how large is the discount?
questions.gold: From 1 November to 31 March, at 30% off the summer rate, with each night priced by its own date (REQ-P4).

questions.question: How must VAT be shown on a Quayline invoice?
questions.gold: At 20%, on its own line under the net total (REQ-P2).

questions.question: How much water must a berth leave under a keel before Quayline may offer it?
questions.gold: At least 0.5 m at the lowest predicted low water of every night of the stay (REQ-S1). A drying berth is the exception: open only to vessels that can take the ground.

questions.question: When do Quayline's cached tide predictions count as too old, and what must happen then?
questions.gold: When the newest prediction was fetched more than 6 hours ago; tidal berths are then not offered at all, because Quayline never guesses a tide (REQ-S2).

questions.question: How quickly must a storm warning reach the boats in a Quayline marina, and how?
questions.gold: By SMS to every vessel on site within 10 minutes of the harbourmaster issuing it (REQ-S3).

questions.question: Where is the check that decides whether a vessel fits a berth in Quayline?
questions.gold: fits() in src/quayline/bookings/allocate.py.

questions.question: Which Quayline function confirms a held booking, and in which file?
questions.gold: confirm_booking in src/quayline/bookings/confirm.py.

questions.question: Where does Quayline turn an amount in pence into a pounds string?
questions.gold: format_gbp in src/quayline/billing/money.py.

questions.question: Which Quayline function decides whether a night is charged at the winter rate?
questions.gold: is_winter in src/quayline/billing/rates.py, used by nightly_rate_pence.

questions.question: Where does Quayline parse the timestamps that come from the tide feed?
questions.gold: parse_feed_time in src/quayline/tides/cache.py.

questions.question: Which Quayline file decides whether a notification goes by email, push or SMS?
questions.gold: src/quayline/notify/channels.py (channels_for).

questions.question: Where are Quayline's default settings, such as the hold length and the clearance margin, kept?
questions.gold: In config/quayline.toml; the environment can override any key as QUAYLINE_<SECTION>_<KEY>.

questions.question: Which Quayline API route records a departure, and what does recording it set off?
questions.gold: POST /v1/stays/{stay_id}/departure in src/quayline/api/routes.py; recording the departure enqueues the stay's invoice job (ADR-0009, on_departure_recorded).

questions.question: When did Quayline start locking the berth row on confirmation, and what incident led to it?
questions.gold: On 2026-03-20, in PR #44 (Lock the berth row while confirming), after berth C3 at Mill Quay was double-booked for 9-12 March (#38).

questions.question: When was Quayline's 02:00 invoice job removed?
questions.gold: On 2026-05-08, by PR #79 (Invoice on departure), which closed #76 and was released in 1.2.0.

questions.question: What stopped Quayline's tide fetch job in February 2026, and what was changed?
questions.gold: On 2026-02-11 the feed sent a time without a seconds field and the job crashed, stopping for 9 hours. The 2026-02-12 commit made parse_feed_time accept both forms, and a bad row is now logged and skipped.

questions.question: Was Quayline's booking hold ever shortened from 15 minutes?
questions.gold: Yes, to 10 minutes on 2026-06-22, reverted on 2026-06-26 because kiosk card payments can take up to 12 minutes when the reader dials again; it is 15 minutes again, as REQ-B3 says.

questions.question: When did Quayline start storing money as integer pence?
questions.gold: On 2026-04-24, with PR #70 (Store amounts as integer pence), which implemented ADR-0008 and closed #52.

questions.question: When did Quayline move routine notifications off SMS?
questions.gold: On 2026-06-12, with PR #102 (Email and push by default, SMS for safety alerts), released in 1.3.0; it implemented ADR-0010 and closed #99.

questions.question: Which change stopped Quayline offering a drying berth to a fin-keel yacht, and when?
questions.gold: PR #91, merged on 2026-05-20: fits() refuses a drying berth unless the vessel can take the ground (can_dry). It fixed #86, where berth E7 was offered to Wren, drawing 1.9 m.

questions.question: In which Quayline release did the visitor waitlist first ship?
Which Quayline issue is about the storm warning that did not reach every boat, and is it fixed?
questions.gold: #169, still open: the 31 August warning reached 50 of 63 vessels. A comment says the second batch of 50 got a 429 from Textwell and raise_for_status stopped the loop, so the last 13 were never sent.

questions.question: Why was the Quayline pull request that added SMS retries not merged?
questions.gold: PR #111 was closed unmerged: Textwell already retries delivery on its side and retrying the POST sends the message twice; the team wanted delivery receipts instead (REQ-S4).

questions.question: In the review of Quayline's berth-locking change, why was NOWAIT not used?
questions.gold: In PR #44 the author answered that waiting is fine because the lock is held for milliseconds, and an error would make the clerk retry by hand.

questions.question: Is there an open Quayline request about liveaboards keeping their waitlist place, and what would it take?
questions.gold: Yes, issue #145 (enhancement, open): a liveaboard who leaves for a refit loses their place. It needs a change to ADR-0007 and has not been started.

questions.question: How large was Quayline's SMS bill for May 2026, and where was it raised?
questions.gold: £310, raised in issue #99 (Too many texts) and cited in ADR-0010.

questions.question: Which rounding did the reviewer ask for when Quayline moved to integer pence, and why?
questions.gold: Round half up, not banker's rounding, because the office's spreadsheet rounds half up (review comment on PR #70, on money.py).

questions.question: What did the Quayline issue about penny differences on invoices report, and how was it closed?
questions.gold: Issue #52: the March reconciliation found 7 invoices a penny out against the card terminal totals. It was closed by PR #70 on 2026-04-24.

questions.question: According to the Quayline issue about the tide feed timing out at night, what was the cause and the fix?
questions.gold: Issue #17: the feed's maintenance window is 01:00-03:00 UTC and allocation called it for every quote. It was fixed by the hourly cache of ADR-0003.

questions.question: How should the test suite be run in the Quayline repository, and why does it matter?
questions.gold: With make test, which sets TZ=Europe/London. Calling pytest directly makes the billing tests that cross the 29 March clock change fail for reasons unrelated to the change (CLAUDE.md).

questions.question: Is the 0.0 m depth seeded for Quayline's berth E7 a mistake?
questions.gold: No. E7 at Eastgate is a drying berth that sits on mud at low water, so 0.0 m is correct and must not be repaired (CLAUDE.md).

questions.question: Should Quayline read the tide feed's times as local time, as the feed's documentation says?
questions.gold: No. The feed labels them local but the values are UTC, and parse_feed_time treats them as UTC; reading them as local showed every low water an hour out after the clocks went forward in March 2026 (CLAUDE.md, the 2026-04-02 commit).

questions.question: During a Quayline tide feed outage, why must the staleness limit not be raised to get bookings going?
questions.gold: The runbook says REQ-S2 exists because a stale table once put a visiting yacht aground; load the authority's tables by hand with quayline tides import instead.

questions.question: What lesson did Quayline record about code that looks for a clash and then writes?
questions.gold: A check followed by a write without a lock is a bug; every path that confirms a booking goes through confirm_booking in src/quayline/bookings/confirm.py (the double-booking postmortem).

questions.question: What should Quayline's billing tests cover, according to the winter-rate postmortem?
questions.gold: Stays that cross 31 March and 1 November; and price per night, never per stay.

questions.question: Are Quayline's invoices still produced in a nightly batch?
questions.gold: No. ADR-0002's 02:00 batch was superseded by ADR-0009; since 2026-05-08 (PR #79) the invoice is built when the departure is recorded and emailed within the hour.

questions.question: Does Quayline send booking confirmations by SMS?
questions.gold: Not any more. ADR-0004 did, but since ADR-0010 (shipped 2026-06-12) confirmations go by email and push, or at the office desk; SMS is for safety alerts only.

questions.question: Was the problem of storm alerts not reaching every boat solved by September 2026?
questions.gold: No. Issue #169 is still open. The 2026-09-03 commit added logging of each alert's recipients and receipts (REQ-S4) but did not fix the stopped batch; the office phones Eastgate by hand.

questions.question: How does Quayline price a stay that runs from 30 March to 2 April?
questions.gold: Each night by its own date: the nights of 30 and 31 March at the winter rate (30% off), 1 April at the summer rate. Before PR #124 (2026-07-15) one rate was chosen for the whole stay from the date of booking.

questions.question: Which of Quayline's architecture decisions have been superseded, and by what?
questions.gold: ADR-0002 (nightly invoice batch) by ADR-0009, and ADR-0004 (SMS for every notification) by ADR-0010.

questions.question: Did Quayline's first release send invoices when a boat left?
questions.gold: No. 1.0.0 (2026-03-02) shipped nightly invoices and SMS notifications; invoicing on departure came in 1.2.0 on 2026-05-08.

questions.question: What p99 latency target does Quayline's booking API have?
questions.gold: Nothing in the repository or its tracker records this.

questions.question: Which cloud provider and region host Quayline's production database?
questions.gold: Nothing in the repository or its tracker records this.

questions.question: Who is on call for Quayline outside office hours?
questions.gold: Nothing in the repository or its tracker records this.

questions.question: What is Quayline's summer nightly rate per metre at North Basin?
questions.gold: Nothing in the repository or its tracker records this.
